title: Jurisdictional Lock: per-customer allow/deny policy and EU-only enforcement adapter
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Add a jurisdictional lock adapter to the smart routing layer that enforces per-customer allowlists/denylists and supports an EU-only enforcement mode. This ticket implements the runtime policy checks, config surface for Console and API, and safe rollout strategy with telemetry for blocked requests and fallback decisions. Goal: prevent cross-border processing for customers who require EU-only handling, provide deterministic deny/allow behaviour, and make policy decisions auditable.
acceptance_criteria: Policy engine exposes per-customer flags: 'eu_only', 'allow_regions', 'deny_regions', and 'allowed_tiers'.
Incoming requests evaluated against policy before routing decision; non-compliant requests are blocked or routed to allowed fallback variants per policy.
Console and API can update per-customer policies and changes propagate to routing layer within 60s.
Audit log entries created for every policy decision with fields: customer_id, request_id, matched_rule, action, timestamp, evaluated_region, routed_variant.
Canary rollout demonstrates zero customer regressions for 5 pilot customers and telemetry thresholds pass (routing-failure-rate < 0.1%).
E2E tests cover: allowlist match, denylist match, eu_only blocked outside EU, fallback to compatible model variant when tier mismatch, and API-level config errors produce 400 with helpful message.
implementation_steps: Design policy schema and storage: extend customer config store with boolean eu_only, lists for allow_regions/deny_regions/allowed_tiers, and rule precedence semantics.
Implement Policy Adapter in routing layer: fast in-memory cache keyed by customer_id with TTL and changefeed to invalidate.
Integrate the adapter with Smart Router decision flow: evaluate policy before cost/latency scoring; short-circuit to 'blocked' or 'fallback' actions.
Add auditable logging: structured events to logging pipeline (ClickHouse/BigQuery) with trace ids and K/V fields.
Expose API endpoints and Console UI hooks for editing policies (PM/Console teams will add UI).
Create canary plan: 1% traffic -> 5% -> 20% for customers who opt into pilot; monitor metrics and rollback criteria.
Add unit/integration tests and a Postman collection for API validation; smoke test against Dedicated and Private deployments.
review_comments: PM Nora Singh: please ensure 'eu_only' implies both compute and logging residency — confirm with Privacy team.

updates: 2025-02-18: Initial spike completed — benchmarked cache lookup 50k req/s with <1ms median overhead (Rajesh). See perf notes in Confluence.
2025-02-24: Schema iteration v2 landed on branch 'feature/jurisdictional-adapter' (PR opened) — added 'allowed_tiers' field to handle tier routing fallbacks.
2025-03-01: Integrated changefeed from config-store; propagation latency measured ~45s in staging (acceptable). Added stricter tests for race conditions.
2025-03-05: Canary pilot onboarded 3 customers (internal and partnership accounts). Observed 0.04% routing-failure due to policy mismatch; investigating mis-specified allowlist entry formats.
qa_plan: Unit tests for policy evaluation precedence (deny overrides allow, explicit allow overrides eu_only false).
Integration tests: routing stack with adapter in front, simulate regions with mock endpoints and assert actions.
Regression: run full canary suite against Dedicated and Private installs, validate audit logs exist and contain required fields.
Manual QA: PM-driven test cases for Console edits, error messages, and edge-case CSV import of allowlist.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Internal testing and security review (complete).
Phase 1: Canary with 3 pilot customers (1% traffic) for 72 hours — monitor routing-failure and audit-log completeness.
Phase 2: Expand to 20% for pilot cohort; enable console UI; gather feedback.
Phase 3: General availability; opt-in for existing customers with migration doc and dry-run mode (log-only) for 7 days before enforcement.
Rollback criteria: sustained increase in client errors >0.5% or missing audit logs for >1% of evaluated requests.
notes: Trade-offs: strong enforcement (block) can cause visible customer errors; dry-run mode recommended to surface config mistakes.
Fallback behavior: when tier mismatch occurs and allowed_tiers contains a compatible variant, route to the nearest allowed tier; otherwise return 403 with guidance.
Private/Dedicated installs: the adapter supports local policy overrides; in air-gapped installs, the changefeed will read from local config store.
